style_prompt.purpose: Rules for how to style this project. Follow every rule exactly whenever you write or edit markup, Tailwind classes, or CSS.

stack.rule: Use only Tailwind CSS. No other styling library, no inline style objects, no CSS-in-JS.
Reference file for code style: src/App.css. Glance at it before styling and copy its way of writing.

where_to_write.rule: Put Tailwind classes directly in the className of .tsx / .ts files. This is the default and the preferred place.

A className with more than 8 utilities (each variant such as max-md:p-[16px] counts as one) is too long. Move its static utilities into a named class in App.css with @apply and use that class in className. Conditional or dynamic parts stay in className.
Name the class in kebab-case after what the element is (.search-bar, .rating-chip), never after how it looks. Keep the utilities in the same order as they were in className.
Shorter class lists stay in className. Use @apply for a shorter list only when the user asks for it.

Never store Tailwind utilities in a .tsx / .ts variable, const, object or default prop value (const navLink = "p-[13px_10px] ..."). Write them as a named class in App.css with @apply and use the class name in className, whatever the length.
Never use important: no ! modifier on a Tailwind class (!py-[11px], max-sm:!rounded-[28px], hover:!bg-...) in className or in @apply, and never write !important in CSS.

To change a value that an App.css class already sets, write a new class instead: a modifier class placed right below the base class in App.css (.input-icon { @apply pl-[40px]; } used as className="input input-icon"), or a separate class / class list for that element without the base class. To hide an element whose class sets display, swap the class: className={isHidden ? 'hidden' : 'product-card'}.
Do not add anything else to App.css: no new Tailwind utilities outside those blocks, no new resets, no new element or id rules.

units.rule: Use px only for every size: font-size, line-height, padding, margin, gap, width, max-width, min-width, radius, border.

forbidden.item: rem, em, vw, vh, svh, dvh, ch, fr
fluid sizing such as clamp(), min(), max() with viewport units
Tailwind spacing scale numbers when a px value is meant (write p-[20px], not p-5)

units.rule: Sizes change per breakpoint by writing a new fixed px value, never by scaling.
units.exception: The only relative value allowed is a percentage on flex-basis, for example basis-[25%] or max-md:basis-[33.33%]. Do not use a percentage for any other property.
Centring an absolute icon or button inside a relative input wrapper with top-[50%] -translate-y-1/2 (or top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2) is allowed. It is positioning, not sizing.

layout.rule: Use flex only. Do not use grid (no grid, grid-cols-*, col-span-*, row-span-*, place-*, grid-template).
Rows and columns: flex, flex-row, flex-col, flex-wrap.
A flex child's width is set ONLY with basis-[N%], plus shrink-0 or min-w-0 when needed.
Never set a flex child's width in px: no basis-[120px], no basis-[calc(...)], no w-[Npx] on a flex child. Images may still use max-w-[Npx].
For N items per row with a gap, round the percentage down so the gaps fit: 4 per row basis-[23%], 3 per row basis-[31%], 2 per row basis-[48%], 1 per row basis-[100%].
Spacing between flex items: gap-[Npx] or gap-x-[Npx] / gap-y-[Npx].

height.rule: Never touch or change an h-[...] that already exists. Leave it exactly as it is.
Let content, padding and flex decide height.

breakpoints.rule: Prefer exactly three breakpoints: lg, md, sm. Use these before any other.

scale.breakpoint: max-lg: applies at 1023px and below (tablet landscape)
max-md: applies at 767px and below (tablet portrait)

breakpoints.rule: Write desktop first: the base class is the desktop value, then override downward with max-lg:, max-md:, max-sm:.
Order the variants in className from largest to smallest: base, max-lg:, max-md:, max-sm:. Each smaller one overrides the larger one.
Only add a variant when the value actually changes. Do not repeat the same value at a smaller breakpoint.
Every value at every breakpoint is a fixed px number. Never scale with %, vw, rem or clamp(). The only percentage allowed is flex-basis.
Use an arbitrary variant such as max-[720px]: only when lg, md and sm cannot do the job. Say why in a short comment.
In App.css, use only @media (min-width: Npx) or @media (max-width: Npx) with px values. Match the lg, md, sm widths: 1024px, 768px, 640px (max-width: 1023px, 767px, 639px).

layout.rule: lg: keep the row, reduce gaps and padding a step.
md: allow flex-wrap, and cut the number of items per row by changing basis-[N%], for example basis-[25%] to max-lg:basis-[33.33%] to max-md:basis-[50%].
sm: switch to flex-col, or one item per row (basis-[100%]), and center with items-center.

spacing.rule: Step padding and gap down by about 4px to 8px per breakpoint, for example p-[20px] max-md:p-[16px] max-sm:p-[12px].

typography.rule: Font size and line height are reduced per screen ONLY through @media queries in src/App.css. See font_size_responsive below. This replaces the old habit of writing max-md:text-[length:..] in className.

media.rule: Images keep their ratio. Do not add h-[...]. Reduce the padding around the image instead, and never change an existing pt-[...] unless asked.

visibility.rule: Hide or show with max-lg:hidden, max-md:hidden or max-sm:hidden. Do not remove content that only matters on desktop without telling the user.

font_size_responsive.description: How font size and line height shrink on smaller screens.
font_size_responsive.rule: Do it only with @media (max-width: ...) blocks in src/App.css. Never write max-lg:, max-md:, max-sm: font-size or leading classes in .tsx / .ts, and never use ! overrides to fight a class from App.css.
Use the same widths as the breakpoints: @media (max-width:1023px) for lg, (max-width:767px) for md, (max-width:639px) for sm.
Inside each @media block put ONLY a :root rule. Nothing else goes in the block: no class selectors, no element selectors, no @apply.
The :root rule inside the @media only reassigns size variables, for example --h2-size: 22px;. Classes already read these variables, so every class using them shrinks by itself.
If the size is an existing value, reuse the existing variable name (--h2-size, --price-lg-size, --btn-size, ...) and only change its value inside the @media. Do not create a duplicate.

If the size is a new value that has no variable yet, first add a named variable to the base :root (for example --size-pill-size: 16px), use it in the class or className, then reassign it inside the @media blocks. Name it after the element and end it with -size.

Line height follows the same way. By default it is calc(var(--x-size)+4px), so it updates when --x-size changes and needs no extra rule. Only if a line height must differ from size plus 4px, add a named variable ending with -leading in the base :root, use it as leading-[var(--x-leading)], and reassign it inside the @media blocks.
Reduce 1px to 2px per breakpoint. Write the blocks from largest to smallest (1023px, then 767px, then 639px) so the smaller one wins.

code_style.description: Copy these patterns from src/App.css. Do not invent other forms.
code_style.rule: Sizes and colors come from the variables in :root, for example var(--card-title-size), var(--ink), var(--primary), var(--line).
Line height is always the font-size variable plus 4px: leading-[calc(var(--x-size)+4px)].
If a size or color is needed in more than one place, add a variable to :root first, then use it.
Font families come from @theme: font-manrope, font-inter, font-satoshi.
Multi-line @apply lists put one utility per line, ending with a semicolon on the last one.

markup.rule: Never use any ARIA attribute: no aria-label, aria-hidden, aria-expanded or any other aria-*, and no role attribute.
An icon-only button or link gets a short title attribute instead, for example title="Remove".
Every img has an alt that describes the picture. Never alt="" and never an img without alt.
Never add loading="lazy" to an img.

before_you_finish.check: No rem, em, vw, vh, fr, fractions, clamp().
Every flex child width is basis-[N%]: no basis-[Npx], no basis-[calc(...)], no w-[Npx] on a flex child.
No aria-* and no role attribute anywhere.
No ! important modifier on any Tailwind class and no !important anywhere; overrides are new classes.
Every img has a descriptive, non-empty alt and no loading="lazy".
No className has more than 8 utilities; longer lists live in a named App.css class.
No Tailwind utilities stored in a .tsx / .ts variable, const, object or default prop; reused class lists are App.css classes.
Responsive overrides use max-lg, max-md, max-sm, written largest to smallest.
No new h-[...] added and no existing h-[...] changed.
Short class lists are in the .tsx / .ts file; only lists of more than 8 utilities (or ones the user asked for) are in App.css with @apply.
Anything added to App.css is only @theme, :root, a class, or a min/max-width @media.
Font sizes, line heights and colors follow the patterns above.
No max-lg / max-md / max-sm font-size or leading classes in .tsx / .ts. Screen-based size changes live only in App.css @media blocks.
Every font-size @media block contains only :root, and only reassigns variables. New sizes have a named variable in the base :root.
